subject: Clarify: billing for streaming + function calls + ensemble models

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Billing details: streaming + functions + ensemble models

Hi Mina —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal asked us to get crystal-clear on how Redwood will bill a couple of patterns before we finalize the PO. I put the examples in the attached PDF but high level questions:

1) Streaming partial tokens: if our app streams intermediate assistant tokens to the client (partial outputs that are later truncated client-side), do you bill the full generated token stream or only the bytes that the client retained?

2) Function calls / tool outputs: when the assistant triggers a function call and the function returns 400 tokens, then the assistant resumes and generates an additional 200 tokens — is the 400 token tool response billable as model output?

3) Ensemble flows: we plan to run a 2-stage flow — a small reranker model that scores 10 candidates, then the generator uses the top candidate. Are both model calls billed fully (reranker tokens + generator tokens)? If so, how do minimums/rounding apply when you have multiple model invocations in a single logical transaction?

We also want to confirm behavior when committed monthly token minimums and negotiated discounts are in place — do those discounts apply per invocation type (chat/generate/embedding) or only aggregated token usage?

Can you send a short set of invoice examples that show the math? That will help procurement.

Appreciate it —
Jenny Park
Head of Procurement, Acme Health
procurement@acmehealth.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Billing details: streaming + functions + ensemble models

Hi Jenny —

Great questions, thanks for the clear examples. Short answers up front:
- Streaming: billed for tokens actually produced by the model runtime (we don’t try to infer client-side truncation). If the model emitted 1,000 tokens and the client only displayed 600, we bill 1,000.
- Function/tool responses: yes — function outputs returned via the model are billed as part of the response token count.
- Ensemble/multi-call flows: each model invocation is billed independently (so reranker tokens + generator tokens). Minimums and rounding apply per invoice line item, which is model-type grouped by our meter (chat/generate/embedding).

That said, for negotiated committed-usage discounts we can provide either:
A) Aggregated discount: discount applies to the total monthly tokens across model types (preferred for BAU workloads).
B) Split discount: different rates per meter (chat vs embeddings) if you want to tie a portion of commitment to a specific usage class.

Attached is a simple invoice sample that shows three scenarios (streaming truncated by client, function output included, and a two-stage rerank+generate). I also flagged the rounded charge lines and the way our minimums (per-month floor) absorb small spikes.

Proposed next step: if Acme is comfortable with aggregated discounted treatment, we can reflect a blended unit price in the quote and show a sample true-up for months under/over the commit. If you prefer split buckets, Kimberly can sketch out the exact per-meter blended rates.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call with procurement and revenue ops to walk the numbers.

Best,

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Adding a couple of notes on rounding and minimums:

- Minimums: Acme's proposed commitment floor (100M tokens/mo) will be applied as a single monthly floor at invoice time. If actual usage < floor, we invoice floor * unit_price and then deduct any pre-paid credit.

- Rounding: token usage within a model invocation is metered at token level then rounded to the nearest billing quantum (we use 1 token quantum). For invoice presentation we roll up to invoice lines and then apply rounding when converting to currency (cents). This prevents sub-cent fractional lines.

- Multi-invocation aggregation: we do NOT reassign tokens between model calls for rounding purposes — each invocation's tokens are added into the aggregate meter for the month. Example (see attached CSV):

  Scenario A (streaming truncate): model produced 1,000 tokens, client kept 600 -> billed 1,000 tokens at chat rate.
  Scenario B (function call): prompt 120 tokens + function response 400 tokens + follow-on 200 tokens -> billed 720 tokens for that request (prompt + function + follow-on).
  Scenario C (rerank + generate): reranker runs on 10 candidates (10 * 50 tokens = 500), generator produces 900 tokens -> billed 1,400 tokens total. If monthly floor = 100M tokens, these all accumulate toward that commitment.

If Acme would like us to pilot an alternate treatment (for example, bill only kept-streamed tokens for a 3-month pilot), we can scope it but it will be outside standard T&Cs and would need a small implementation fee and a limited-term contract clause.

Kimberly
Director, Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Billing details: streaming + functions + ensemble models

Mina / Kim —

Quick ops confirmation for negotiation: billing will be implemented as follows if we proceed with aggregated-discount quote (what we recommend):

1) Metering: Token counts are emitted by the runtime per invocation and labeled by meter (chat, generate, embedding).
2) Aggregation: Monthly totals are the sum of all invocation counts per meter. For the aggregated discount, we apply the blended per-token price across the total token sum.
3) Minimums: If monthly total < committed floor, invoice shows floor charge and a line-item credit for pre-paid commitment (if applicable).
4) Edge: function/tool outputs included in token counts; streaming truncation is not re-evaluated by server (we cannot see client-side truncation reliably).

If Acme asks for a pilot change to bill only retained streamed tokens or to prorate function outputs differently, we need a signed SOW outlining the narrow scope and a two-month implementation lead time to add signal hooks into our CDN/runtime.

Sergio — tagging you for any legal/partner implications if they ask the marketplace to enforce a different behavior.

Thanks,
Karthik
Revenue Operations
